'''Thompson:''' {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Nancy Landon Kassebaum|Nancy Kassebaum]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Pat Roberts]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsKS}} The '''1996 United States Senate election in Kansas''' was held November 5, 1996. Incumbent Republican U.S. Senator [[Nancy Landon Kassebaum|Nancy Kassebaum]] decided to retire instead of seeking a fourth term. Republican [[Pat Roberts]] won the open seat. [[Term limits in the United States|Term limits]] were an issue during the campaign; while Roberts said that he was not totally opposed to term limits, he was wary of limits that did not apply to current members of Congress, saying that the proposed limits should apply to everyone. While Thompson signed the national term limits pledge from the group [[Americans for Limited Government|Americans for Limited Terms]], Roberts declined to do so, becoming the only major party candidate for the U.S. Senate in the [[United States Senate elections, 1996|1996 elections]] to not sign the pledge.{{cite news | url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19960925&id=QjczAAAAIBAJ&sjid=XucFAAAAIBAJ&pg=6637,4661878 | title = Roberts sole candidate to resist term limits tide | publisher=Lawrence Journal-World | date=September 25, 1996 | access-date=October 15, 2014}} However, he did say that "I plan only to serve two terms in the U.S. Senate."{{cite news | url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/andrewkaczynski/pat-roberts-said-he-in-1996-hed-serve-2-terms-in-senate-hes | title = Pat Roberts Said In 1996 He'd Only Serve Two Terms — He's Running For His Fourth | publisher=BuzzFeed | date=October 14, 2014 | access-date=October 15, 2014}} In 2014, he was [[2014 United States Senate election in Kansas|re-elected]] to a fourth and final term in office, before retiring in [[2020 United States Senate election in Kansas|2020]]. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== * [[Sally Thompson]], [[Kansas State Treasurer]] ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic Party primary results{{Cite web|url=http://www.kssos.org/elections/96elec/96sum/p96ussum.html|title=1996 Primary Election US Senate Races}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Sally Thompson | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 121,476 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 121,476 | percentage= 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== * [[Pat Roberts]], U.S. Representative * Tom Little * Tom Oyler * Richard L.
